These examples should clearly highlight how to avoid stepping onto fire tiles placed near the corridor edges. In addition to these, you should provide alternative demonstrations where the left-edge corridor is used, especially in cases where the top-edge corridor is blocked by fire, so the agent learns to adapt to different safe paths. It is also beneficial to include variations of these demonstrations starting from multiple positions with different fire configurations, helping the agent generalize fire avoidance strategies. By expanding the demonstration suite in this way, the agent's policy can better handle randomized or partially obstructed corridors safely.
